mainEntity.name: How much does a Kia Sportage 2.0 CRDi & 1.7 CRDi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Kia Sportage 2.0 CRDi & 1.7 CRDi engine typically costs £695-£1,795 for supply-only, depending on the specific engine code (D4FD, D4HA, or D4HB) and condition. Supply & fit labour adds approximately £395-£650.

mainEntity.name: What is the most reliable engine code for the Kia Sportage 2.0 CRDi & 1.7 CRDi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The D4HB 2.0L CRDi Euro 6 diesel is widely considered the most reliable, offering proven durability when maintained properly. Later QL and NQ5 generation units benefit from refined timing components and improved emissions systems that address earlier D4HA concerns.

mainEntity.name: Is the Kia Sportage 2.0 CRDi & 1.7 CRDi timing chain problem really that bad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, D4HA timing chain tensioner wear is a documented issue on Kia Sportage 2.0 CRDi & 1.7 CRDi models, typically appearing between 80,000-120,000 miles. Early rattling on cold starts is the key warning sign before catastrophic failure occurs.

mainEntity.name: Will a Kia Sportage 2.0 CRDi & 1.7 CRDi D4HB engine pass ULEZ?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Kia Sportage 2.0 CRDi & 1.7 CRDi models fitted with the D4HB Euro 6 diesel engine are ULEZ compliant and exempt from London and other UK clean air zone charges. Verify your vehicle's Euro 6 status via the DVLA or TfL checker before purchasing a replacement.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my Kia Sportage 2.0 CRDi & 1.7 CRDi engine after a major failure?

acceptedAnswer.text: For major failures like seized components or lost compression, replacing your Kia Sportage 2.0 CRDi & 1.7 CRDi engine with a rebuilt unit is usually more cost-effective than attempting an in-situ repair. Rebuilt engines include upgraded parts addressing the original failure point plus warranty protection.

historyTimeline.h2: Kia Sportage 2.0 CRDi & 1.7 CRDi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 2.0 CRDi and 1.7 CRDi diesel variants launched, they formed the backbone of the Sportage range, prioritising fuel economy, low running costs, and towing capability. Over time, these units evolved from the early SL generation's D4FD and D4HA codes to the refined, Euro 6-compliant D4HB found in modern QL and NQ5 models.

milestones.description: D4FD (1.7L, 115hp) and D4HA (2.0L, 136hp) introduced on the SL generation, establishing the core CRDi diesel lineup for the UK market.
D4HB (2.0L, 185hp) Euro 6 diesel introduced on the QL generation, adding AdBlue SCR technology for ULEZ compliance and improved refinement.
D4HB carried over to the NQ5 generation with refined Euro 6d emissions mapping, updated engine management, and enhanced thermal efficiency.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Kia Sportage 2.0 CRDi & 1.7 CRDi is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Kia Sportage 2.0 CRDi & 1.7 CRDi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Kia Sportage 2.0 CRDi and 1.7 CRDi diesel engines are generally robust, but high-mileage UK examples commonly face issues with timing chain wear (D4HA), turbo actuators (D4FD), and AdBlue systems (D4HB). Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the Kia Sportage 2.0 CRDi & 1.7 CRDi D4HA Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Timing chain tensioners lose hydraulic pressure over time, allowing chain slack that causes rattling and potential valve-to-piston contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides and seals before catastrophic failure occurs.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable only if caught early with rattling symptoms; prevents major engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine with upgraded tensioner, bench-tested, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Best value when chain has jumped or compression is lost; restores full reliability.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2010-2015 Kia Sportage 2.0 CRDi & 1.7 CRDi is worth ~£4,000-£7,000. If the vehicle is worth under £5,000, a targeted chain kit repair or used engine typically makes more financial sense than a full rebuilt unit. For vehicles worth £5,000-£8,000, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine is a viable investment if you plan to keep the car 2+ years.
problems.recommendation: If your Sportage shows early chain rattle on cold start but still runs smoothly, a preventative chain kit replacement from a specialist offers strong value. However, once timing has jumped or compression is lost, replacement with a rebuilt unit is more cost-effective than attempting an in-situ repair.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt D4HA Kia Sportage 2.0 CRDi & 1.7 CRDi engine prices

problems.h4: Turbo Actuator Failure - Boost Pressure Loss on the Kia Sportage 2.0 CRDi & 1.7 CRDi D4FD
problems.rootCause: Electronic turbo actuators suffer from heat fatigue and internal motor wear, causing erratic boost control, reduced power, and eventual turbo seizure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace faulty turbo actuator unit, recalibrate boost mapping, road test.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if turbo core is undamaged and no metal contamination has occurred.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine with refurbished or upgraded turbo, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Essential if actuator failure caused turbo seizure or metal debris entered cylinders.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2010-2015 Kia Sportage 1.7 CRDi is worth ~£3,500-£6,500. If the vehicle is worth under £5,000, evaluate if a standalone actuator repair or used engine is more economical. For vehicles worth £5,000+, a rebuilt engine provides long-term reliability and warranty protection.
problems.recommendation: If your Sportage shows intermittent boost loss but no unusual noises, actuator replacement alone may resolve the issue affordably. However, if you hear grinding from the turbo or see metal flakes in the oil, a rebuilt engine with a refurbished turbo is the only safe, warranty-backed solution.
